decisions.executionNote: The board shows a purple cup. Begin raising and pitching both wrists toward downward grasps; left will lift the basket before right picks the target.
Advance left above the moving basket with open fingers while completing downward wrist pitch. Right stays clear on its side.
Align the left downward gripper across the basket's left rim, tracking its rightward belt motion. Descend cautiously; right remains clear.
Track the basket rim slightly right, settle around its upper side, and close the left fingers. Retention will be checked during a small lift.
Test and establish basket retention by lifting the closed left gripper 12 cm. Move right toward a safe conveyor interception pose, keeping arms separated.
Basket slipped and tilted rather than following the lift. Reopen left and reposition over its accessible left end for a deeper grasp; keep right out of its way.
Reattempt retention at the elevated left corner of the tilted basket, staying on the left side of the robot. Close only after centering the corner.
Continuity guard stopped the outward approach. Replan with smaller inward/downward increments to put the basket corner between the fingers without extending farther.
Close and lift the basket corner while retracting toward the left workspace to preserve elbow-up reach margin. Check whether the basket actually follows.

The basket is not retained and has moved into the right workspace. Switch roles without crossing: right prepares to recover basket, left approaches the purple cup but will not pick before basket lift.
Right approaches the exposed upper basket corner with fingers open. Left aligns above the moving purple cup without closing yet.
Bring right fingers behind and down around the visible basket corner, then close. Hold left open over the cup, allowing belt motion to center it.
The basket rim remains left of the right fingers. Reopen, shift left within the right workspace to straddle it, and close again; lift left slightly clear of the rolling cup.
Finish closing right, then test basket retention with an 11 cm vertical lift. Left tracks above the purple cup while staying open.
Basket did not follow the last lift. Reopen right and align the wrist-view corner centrally with a deeper approach, without crossing the centerline. Left continues tracking the cup.
The right wrist now shows the basket corner between the open fingers. Close at this alignment and make a small retention test; left recenters above the target cup.
Refine right alignment slightly toward the white rim and descend deeper before closing. The corner appears not yet securely retained. Keep left over the conveyor target.
Settle the right closure around the now-centered rim, then lift 9 cm with slight retraction. Left remains open and tracks the target.
Rim again stayed fixed. Reposition right nearer the robot so the corner lies at the finger pads rather than behind them, then close at a lower height. Left tracks the purple cup.
Settle closure and test right basket lift again. Left descends open around the passing purple cup while retracting to maintain reach margin.
Right adjusts a centimeter toward the rim and descends farther with open fingers. Left closes around the centered purple cup before it passes beyond the left workspace.
Lift and retract the left cup grasp to verify retention. Change the right approach angle and rise clear of the tilted basket to acquire its rim from the near side.
The purple cup was not retained. Prioritize a stable basket grasp: right shifts the visible corner from left of the jaws into their center and descends slightly with the new angled approach.
Seat the right angled fingers around the visible central basket corner, close with a settling pause, then test a small upward movement.
Test the deeper angled basket grip with a 14 cm lift and gentle retraction/pitch adjustment. Watch whether the basket follows rather than relying on gripper state.
Reapproach the basket corner from above with restored downward orientation, keeping the rim at the finger pads rather than beneath the gripper body.
Close right at the higher, head-view rim alignment and allow full settling before lifting. This avoids the previous too-deep corner approaches.
Test the higher rim grasp with a 12 cm lift and slight inward retraction. Keep the right gripper closed and inspect whether the basket follows.
Replan from the interrupted lift with inward/downward margin. Keep the rim closed and gently rotate the tilted basket toward an upright opening, checking retention visually.
Use smaller increments after the continuity interruption. Ease the basket away from the near edge while slowly correcting its tilt; left withdraws for clearance.
No motion executed on the last rejection. Make a small orientation recovery toward the last accepted target and release the wedged right fingers, then pause to settle.
Recenter the basket's vertical rim between the right pads after releasing the wedge. Close only after the small leftward alignment, leaving the left arm clear.
The head view still places the basket corner outside the left right-hand finger. Open and shift farther left within the right workspace, correcting wrist tilt to put the corner inside the jaw span.
Use the now-clear wrist view to straddle the basket's narrow upper rim: a small right/down correction, then close and settle without immediate lifting.
Allow right closure to finish on the centered rim, then make a straight 6 cm retention test without additional rotation or lateral dragging.
Replan from the guard interruption. The rim is ahead of the right fingertips in the wrist view; reopen and advance toward it while slightly lowering, rather than repeating a closure behind it.
Lower the open right pads to the basket rim now centered in both views, with a slight near-side correction. Previous high closures appeared above the rim.
Close and settle at the rim now directly between the right finger tips. Make only a 12 mm lift test before committing to a larger basket lift.
Continue a slow closed-gripper basket lift, adding 7 cm while retracting slightly for reach margin. Inspect whether the basket remains coupled to the right hand.
The basket stayed in place. Correct both the forward and vertical miss at the rim: advance open right fingers farther over the upper corner and lower below its edge before closing.
Make a final small near/down correction to surround the visible basket corner, then close and settle without lifting. Retention is still uncertain.
Finish settling the right fingers around the visible thin rim, then test a slow 6 cm lift with minimal lateral motion.
The rim still is not retained. Change to the basket's protruding handle on the near-right side, moving clear with open fingers and restoring a downward approach.
The basket handle is now visible between the right open pads. Make a small right/near alignment and close on the loop, keeping the left arm clear.
Basket settled lower and is not held. Open right, move toward the near-side handle, and descend to its new height rather than closing above it.
The basket has rotated upright. Center right pads on the now-visible handle segment, close gently, and settle before testing retention.
The basket fell clear of the hand and is not retained. Open right and cautiously approach its lower resting position while preserving elbow-up configuration; left stays safely clear.
Withdraw the right gripper from the conveyor rail and move laterally toward the fallen basket, lowering only slightly while checking configuration and reach clearance.
The lower approach failed IK, so abandon that suffix and raise right to recover elbow-up reach margin and clear the rail. The basket and target have not been secured.
Try a modest near-side wrist angle for the fallen basket, lowering only 3 cm while monitoring IK continuity and maintaining the same elbow-up branch.
The lower wrist angle triggered a large IK branch jump. Replan from the observed pose and recover upward to a continuous elbow-up posture instead of forcing the fallen-basket reach.
Clear the conveyor rail and return both hands toward safe separated hover poses. The fallen basket is below the demonstrated continuous reach and the purple target is no longer visible.
Complete the safe separated hover recovery and monitor the belt. Neither object is retained; avoid another rejected low reach or collision with the conveyor rail.
Hold both open grippers in safe separated elbow-up poses and monitor for a recoverable target. The basket is below the conveyor and the purple cup is no longer visible; completion is not established.
Maintain safe separated elbow-up hover while monitoring the empty conveyor. Neither basket nor target is retained; avoid forcing the previously rejected low reach.
